response.query: Which quantitative dose and fidelity metrics (proportion of planned posts delivered, response latency, moderator adherence scores, participant engagement thresholds) and cutoffs should determine progression?
response.answer: For progression, metrics like 80% delivery of planned posts, response latency under 24 hours, 90% moderator adherence, and 70% participant engagement thresholds are essential. Cutoffs should be set at these levels for effective evaluation.

results.title: Measurement Guidance Toolkit - National Mentoring Resource Center
results.content: Please use the links to the left to navigate the domains and recommended measures for outcomes within each domain. Learn more about the development and contents of the Toolkit and how this resource can help your program’s evaluation efforts. While this Toolkit can help your mentoring program measure many outcomes more effectively, the recommended instruments will be most effective if used within the context of a well-designed evaluation plan. It should be kept in mind, furthermore, that the instruments are likely to lose their value if they are changed (excepting the potential modifications that are discussed in the Toolkit for selected measures), administered incorrectly, or used in contexts where the desired outcomes are apt to be elusive due to poor program implementation or an insufficient theory of change driving program activities. In 2018, we added measures of relationship quality and characteristics, as assessing these factors can help ensure that youth are receiving appropriate support and that their mentoring relationships are progressing as intended and are likely to result in positive outcomes in relevant domains.
